findings.evidence: WAL-logged, crash-safe e MVCC de graça pelo próprio PostgreSQL
findings.message: Consistency claim at the edges→CSR data-flow seam invites the wrong inference: 'MVCC de graça' is true of the theodb.graph_csr catalog row, but traversal results (graph_expand/graph_ppr/graph_rag_search) are served from the CSR frozen at graph_build/graph_refold time — committed edge INSERTs after the build are silently invisible to every traversal until an explicit graph_refold, with no staleness signal (the per-backend cache keyed by built_at, graph.rs:17-20, only invalidates on refold — it never detects new edges). The lakehouse doc handles the analogous seam with an explicit freshness contract (theodb.htap_freshness); this doc offers refold (§4) but never states the silent-staleness failure mode.
findings.remediation: Add an operational note: traversal reflects the CSR as of the last graph_build/graph_refold — new committed edges are invisible until refold; there is no freshness function, so schedule refold after ingest.

findings.evidence: (`#[pg_extern]` em `theodb_rs/src/graph.rs:334-493`, wrappers `theodb.*` em `theodb_rs/src/graph.rs:551-589`)
findings.message: 20 `graph*.rs:NNN` line-number references spread across nearly every section ('Verificado em ...:NNN' after each function), including a range pin `graph.rs:334-493`, versus the 0-2 header-only convention of docs/features/01-12. Each pin is a rot site invalidated by any edit above it in the file; with no verified-at commit marker the doc cannot signal staleness (rot-resistance principle: reference stable symbols, not line offsets).
findings.remediation: Confine line pins to the Status header and reference functions by symbol name (`graph_build` em `graph.rs`) in section bodies.

findings.evidence: Instala a extensão `theodb` (own-code), que provê os catálogos `theodb.graph_csr` / `theodb.graph_nodes` / `theodb.graph_edges` e todas as funções `theodb.graph_*` ... [vs 15-lakehouse-parquet.md:30] Instala a extensão `theodb` e sua base `theodb_rs` via `CASCADE` [vs theodb.control] requires = 'theodb_rs'
findings.message: SSoT violation: the extension boundary is stated inconsistently across the doc set. Docs 13:31, 14:37, 17:34 and 19:33 attribute catalogs/AMs/functions directly to the extension 'theodb' ('Instala a extensão theodb (own-code), que provê...'), while docs 15:30 and 16:31 correctly state the two-extension layering ('Instala a extensão theodb e sua base theodb_rs via CASCADE'). The repo's actual layout confirms the latter: theodb.control declares requires = 'theodb_rs', and every cited symbol (#[pg_extern] in theodb_rs/src/graph.rs, am/mod.rs, etc.) belongs to the base extension theodb_rs, not to the SQL wrapper extension theodb. The same architectural fact restated in two divergent formulations across 7 sibling docs is a divergence bomb: a reader debugging '\dx' output or a DROP EXTENSION cascade gets two different mental models depending on which page they read.
findings.remediation: Standardize the section-1 boilerplate across all 7 docs on the accurate two-extension formulation used by docs 15/16 (theodb + base theodb_rs via CASCADE).

findings.evidence: SELECT theodb.graph_build('friendship', 'src', 'dst');
findings.message: Doc-code contract: every function documented on this page is `REVOKE ALL ... FROM PUBLIC` in the extension SQL (theodb.graph_* at graph.rs:568-577; ai.extract_entities/ai.extract_graph/theodb.graph_upsert at graph_extract.rs:374-376; theodb.graph_embed_nodes/graph_rag_search at graph_rag.rs:97-98; theodb.embed at api.rs:472), yet the page never states the privilege requirement. A non-superuser (or any role without an explicit GRANT) following the doc gets `permission denied` on every example. The sibling doc (15-lakehouse-parquet.md § 2) documents the same REVOKE pattern explicitly — this page omits it.
findings.remediation: Add a security note (mirroring 15-lakehouse-parquet.md § 2) stating the graph/extract/GraphRAG surface is revoked from PUBLIC and requires superuser or an explicit GRANT.

findings.evidence: bash scripts/docs-features-lint.sh: pre-fix 'FAIL [573f6c402ab07757] unaliased SELECT node FROM theodb.graph_expand' exit=1; post-fix 'PASS [573f6c402ab07757] graph_expand example is aliased' exit=0. Example now: SELECT t.node FROM theodb.graph_expand(...) AS t(node) — matches RETURNS SETOF bigint contract (graph.rs:557).
findings.message: Doc-code contract violation: the example errors when copied verbatim. `theodb.graph_expand` RETURNS SETOF bigint (theodb_rs/src/graph.rs:557), so in FROM its default output column is named `graph_expand`, not `node` — `SELECT node FROM theodb.graph_expand(...)` fails with `ERROR: column "node" does not exist`. The extension's own SQL proves this: graph_rag.rs:85 must alias it `AS t(node_id)` to name the column.
findings.remediation: Alias the SRF: `SELECT t.node FROM theodb.graph_expand('friendship', ARRAY[4]::bigint[], 1) AS t(node);` (or `SELECT graph_expand FROM ...`).

findings.evidence: bash scripts/docs-features-lint.sh: pre-fix 'FAIL [d2d823232022541a] no UPDATE/DELETE typed-error caveat' exit=1; post-fix 'PASS [d2d823232022541a] discloses INSERT-only DML contract' exit=0. Caveat (4) added citing columnar.rs:15/:237 typed-error stubs.

findings.evidence: bash scripts/docs-features-lint.sh: pre-fix 'FAIL [52f0c1037a2d1133] claims projected-only decode' exit=1; post-fix 'PASS [52f0c1037a2d1133] seqscan decode-all + m99 measured limit disclosed' exit=0. §4 now states decode of ALL columns (columnar.rs:1015-1021), parity-or-slower vs heap with m99-columnar-tam.md linked, projection gains only via M100 CustomScan.
findings.message: Data-flow claim at the TAM seam is false and contradicts the project's own recorded limit (honest-limits principle). The doc states a plain SELECT decodes only projected columns, but the plain seqscan path decodes ALL columns of every stripe (theodb_rs/src/am/columnar.rs:1015-1021 — load_next_batch builds coldesc for 0..natts and decode_stripe over the full tupdesc; projection pushdown exists only in the M100 CustomScan path via read_stripe_columns' projection arg, columnar.rs:697-709). The project's own benchmark docs/benchmarks/m99-columnar-tam.md records plain seqscan as 'at parity-or-slower than heap, by design' (~16-26x slower measured) precisely because 'a plain seqscan receives no projection'. Presenting this as 'a forma de uso padrão' without the measured slowdown misleads operators.
findings.remediation: Rewrite §4: plain seqscan decodes all columns and is measured parity-or-slower than heap (link m99-columnar-tam.md); projection/vectorization gains require the M100 CustomScan path (GUC on + admitted forms).

findings.message: The `theodb.enable_columnar_agg` 'default OFF' fact is restated 4 times (lines 18-19, 92-94, 285, 299). If the default ever flips to ON (a plausible graduation of an opt-in), four sites must change in lockstep — duplication of a single volatile configuration fact.

findings.evidence: "`count(*)` é a forma mais simples admitida (kind 0 em `theodb_rs/src/am/columnar_agg.rs:328`). Responde do metadado colunar sem materializar linhas." — vs code df_executor.rs:245: "proj.push(0); // count(*) needs a column to establish the row count"
findings.message: Pattern 'metadata-only aggregate fast-path' — verdict: misapplied-in-doc. The doc claims count(*) (kind 0) 'responde do metadado colunar sem materializar linhas', but the code has no metadata fast-path for count(*): theodb_rs/src/am/df_executor.rs:199 builds a DataFusion `count(lit(1))` expression and :245 explicitly projects column 0 because 'count(*) needs a column to establish the row count' — i.e. the scan decodes at least one column's chunks into Arrow batches and DataFusion counts the rows. The genuine directory-only (metadata) fast-path exists ONLY for min/max (kinds 6/7, directory_minmax — correctly described in the doc's section 13). Attributing the metadata-only shape to count(*) transfers the min/max pattern to an aggregate that actually runs the vectorized decode path.
findings.remediation: Reword section 6 to say count(*) runs via the vectorized CustomScan (decodes one column, no PG tuple materialization) — reserve 'respondido só do metadado/diretório' for the min/max fast-path of section 13.

findings.evidence: Rust (DataFusion + Arrow, Apache-2.0) — **sem DuckDB** (o `pg_duckdb`, último componente C++/httpfs do projeto, foi **removido por completo** no M143)
findings.message: Missing scaling/deployment limit at the I/O seam: the doc announces removal of the 'último componente C++/httpfs' but never states the consequence — the own-code Parquet path reads/writes the server-local filesystem only (theodb_rs/src/parquet.rs:60: object_store LocalFileSystem). A 'lakehouse' surface is normally expected to reach object storage (s3://, gs://); after the httpfs removal there is no remote-path support, and every example silently assumes a local server path. Operators planning object-store lakehouses need this limit documented (honest-limits principle).
findings.remediation: State explicitly that v1 Parquet I/O is server-local filesystem only (LocalFileSystem, parquet.rs:60) — no s3:// or object-store paths — and mark remote object-store support as follow-on.

findings.evidence: ALTER SYSTEM SET theodb.embedding_api_key  = 'sk-...';
findings.message: The documented credential-provisioning example `ALTER SYSTEM SET theodb.embedding_api_key = '...'` (repeated in the full-flow at line 311) persists the API key in plaintext in postgresql.auto.conf and, when log_statement/pgaudit is enabled, records the literal key in the server log and in the operator's client history (CWE-312 cleartext storage / CWE-532 insertion of sensitive information into log file). The mechanism itself matches the project's sanctioned posture (GucContext::Suset, value hidden from non-superusers, dead-letter redaction — all correctly documented in this same file), but the doc gives no caveat that the SET statement/auto.conf can expose the key outside that GUC protection. Placeholder 'sk-...' is not a real secret (verified — no live credential in the diff).
findings.remediation: Add a one-line caveat next to both occurrences (lines 40 and 311): ensure postgresql.auto.conf file permissions, avoid log_statement='all' during key provisioning (or rotate after), and never commit the statement to versioned scripts.

findings.evidence: o worker é **um por servidor** e fixado ao banco `postgres` (`WORKER_DBNAME = "postgres"` — `theodb_rs/src/vectorizer.rs:662`). Um launcher multi-DB dirigido por GUC é follow-up.
findings.message: Worker-lifecycle caveat is stated but its failure mode is not: the honesty note says the single worker is fixed to database 'postgres' (verified: WORKER_DBNAME = "postgres", theodb_rs/src/vectorizer.rs:662), yet the doc never spells out the consequence — a vectorizer declared in any other database enqueues jobs that are NEVER drained (silent pending accumulation), the exact failure shape the doc does warn about for the missing shared_preload_libraries case ('a fila acumula jobs pending mas nada os drena'). Symmetric disclosure of the same backpressure failure mode is missing for the wrong-database case.
findings.remediation: Extend the note: vectorizers declared in databases other than 'postgres' accumulate pending jobs that are never processed in v1.

findings.evidence: "Jobs concluídos são **removidos** (à la `pgmq.archive`), não retidos — a tabela fica enxuta."
findings.message: Pattern 'queue done-job disposal' — verdict: applied_correctly with an imprecise analogy. The shape claim matches the code (done jobs are DELETEd; theodb_rs/src/vectorizer.rs dead-letter purge comment: '`done` jobs are already DELETEd; this bounds the retained `failed` history'). However the analogy 'à la `pgmq.archive`' names the wrong pgmq operation: pgmq.archive RETAINS the message in an archive table, while pgmq.delete removes it — the TheoDB behavior corresponds to pgmq.delete. Advisory only; the described code shape itself is correct.
findings.remediation: Change the analogy to 'à la pgmq.delete' or drop the pgmq reference.

findings.message: Inconsistent component status across the doc set: doc 17's banner classifies theodb_symqg as 'AM alternativo / experimental' and 'não é o default recomendado' (hnsw 2.6-3.9x faster, gate NOT met), while doc 19 presents it neutrally as one of 'os três access methods own-code theodb_ivfflat / theodb_hnsw / theodb_symqg' under a blanket '✅ Entregue' status, with only a bare link to the E2 verdict in §11.
